name: DayFront
description: DayFront is the open-source CalDAV frontend for calendars and tasks. Connect it to an existing standards-compliant CalDAV server and let each user sign in with their own CalDAV credentials.

paths.name: Persistent Session Data
paths.description: Stores the generated session secret so users remain signed in across updates and restarts.

paths.name: Advanced Configuration Directory
paths.description: Optional directory containing config.yaml for advanced settings and external calendar subscriptions.

ports.name: Web UI Port
ports.description: DayFront HTTP port. Use HTTPS through a trusted reverse proxy when exposing DayFront outside a trusted LAN.

variables.name: CalDAV Server URL
variables.description: Full HTTP or HTTPS URL of the CalDAV server.

variables.name: Authentication Mode
variables.description: Prompts each user for their own CalDAV credentials. Existing containers without this setting continue using legacy single-account mode.

variables.name: Session Secret File
variables.description: File where DayFront generates and retains its encrypted-login session key. Change only when using a custom data mapping.

variables.name: Session Lifetime
variables.description: Maximum login-session lifetime in hours. The default is 720 hours (30 days).

variables.name: Container Timezone
variables.description: System timezone used for container logs and runtime behavior, for example UTC or America/Toronto.

variables.name: Calendar Display Timezone
variables.description: Timezone used to display and interpret calendar values. Use local for each browser's timezone, UTC, or an IANA name such as America/Toronto.

variables.name: Time Display Format
variables.description: Time display format. Use 12h for AM/PM or 24h for 24-hour time.

variables.name: Sidebar Open by Default
variables.description: Set true to open the sidebar when DayFront loads; false starts with the calendar maximized.

variables.name: Trust Reverse Proxy
variables.description: Set true only when DayFront is directly behind a trusted proxy that overwrites forwarded headers.
